title: The Playlist of the quarry
premise: When Coral Vasquez inherits his late grandmother's recipe box, he discovers index cards hidden among the recipes that document decades of chemical dumping by the quarry company that funds half of Marrow Creek — including the school. The school board buried the findings years ago, and his grandmother, the school's former cafeteria cook, had been quietly collecting proof. As Coral decodes her coded notes with help from an unlikely found family of misfits, he must decide whether protecting the town's fragile economy is worth the truth about why so many residents are sick. In the end, Coral publishes the evidence at the spring festival, forcing resignations and a cleanup settlement, and finally claims his place in a community that sees him fully.
about_author: Noor Blackwood grew up in a small quarry town where everyone knew everyone's business except their own history. They write stories about quiet kids who find loud courage, and about the families we build when the ones we're given keep secrets.

chapters.title: Cardamom and Concrete
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At Grandma Rosa's funeral, Coral receives her recipe box and retreats into routine: school, silence, invisibility as the only out kid in Marrow Creek. Emotional beat: grief wrapped in numbness, and the ache of being known by only one person who's now gone.

chapters.title: The Card Between the Cakes
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Sorting the recipe box, Coral finds an index card reading 'Quarry water, 1979 — ask Delia M.' between cake recipes, written in code. He assumes it's a mistake until he finds three more cards hidden in the dividers. Emotional beat: curiosity cracking open grief.

chapters.title: Locker Shut, Head Down
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A normal school day establishes the stakes: the quarry company sponsors the science wing, the board president is beloved, and Coral keeps his identity sealed tight. He almost throws the cards away. Emotional beat: the exhausting cost of staying small.

chapters.title: Delia M. Has a Grandson
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral tracks down Delia Mercado, a retired nurse, who goes pale at the card and slams her door — but not before saying 'Your grandmother was braver than this town deserved.' Emotional beat: first confirmation the secret is real and dangerous.

chapters.title: The Detention Table
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Stuck in after-school detention on a truancy technicality, Coral meets Priya (arson-adjacent troublemaker), Wes (expelled quarterback), and Junie (hacker caught changing grades). Their banter cracks something open in him. Emotional beat: reluctant warmth, the first spark of belonging.

chapters.title: Decoding Rosa
chapters.summary: Group POV rotating through the four. At the diner, the crew helps crack Rosa's cipher — recipe measurements map to dates, locations, and names of sick workers. Coral realizes she documented everything alone for thirty years. Emotional beat: awe and guilt at how lonely her vigil was.

chapters.title: What the Water Tastes Like
chapters.summary: Wes's POV. Wes admits his little brother's illness was never explained; his family lives downstream of the quarry. He joins not for justice but fury. Emotional beat: loyalty to family colliding with loyalty to town.

chapters.title: The Board President's Smile
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral interviews school board chair Hal Brandt for the school paper as cover. Hal is charming, generous, and lies smoothly about a 1994 'environmental review.' Coral notices the framed photo: Hal and Rosa, arm in arm, 1996. Emotional beat: dread beneath politeness.

chapters.title: Junie Goes Digging
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. Junie pulls old county records and finds the 1994 review was falsified — signed by Rosa herself. The group fractures: was Rosa complicit or coerced? Emotional beat: betrayal, and the question of whether heroes are allowed flaws.

chapters.title: The Recipe for Coercion
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Among the cards Coral finds one addressed to him: 'If you're reading this, mijo, they'll say I lied. Check the second tin.' In a rusted cookie tin: Rosa's sworn affidavit, never filed, describing threats against her family. Emotional beat: posthumous embrace from beyond the grave.

chapters.title: Someone Slashed the Tires
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. After the group requests public records, Priya's car is slashed and an anonymous note warns them off. Fear splits the crew — Wes wants out, Junie wants to go public now, Priya wants proof first. Emotional beat: found family tested by real danger.

chapters.title: Spring Festival Countdown
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The town announces the Quarry Centennial Festival where Hal will receive a civic award — and the quarry's expansion permit will be rubber-stamped. Deadline established: expose everything before the vote. Emotional beat: ticking clock tightening every scene.

chapters.title: Rosa's Kitchen, Reopened
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Cooking from Rosa's actual recipes, Coral finds a final card sewn into the box lining naming the dump sites and a witness still alive: Delia Mercado. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose; the kitchen becomes headquarters.

chapters.title: Delia's Testimony
chapters.summary: Delia's POV (first time). Delia confesses: as the quarry's contract nurse she logged contamination cases for years until Hal bought her silence with her grandson's college tuition. She agrees to speak — if Coral protects her name. Emotional beat: shame meeting absolution.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. Someone uploads a partial scan of the cards online, stripped of context; Hal spins it as a grieving kid's fabrication. Coral is publicly humiliated at school, outed by rumor in the process. Emotional beat: betrayal within the group and the cruelest exposure yet.

chapters.title: Who Sold Us Out
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The group turns on each other hunting the leak, until Wes confesses he showed the cards to his parents hoping for help — and his father called Hal. Emotional beat: forgiveness as a choice, not a feeling; the family nearly shatters and holds.

chapters.title: Ninety-Six Hours
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. With the permit vote Friday and Hal threatening restraining orders, the crew plans to present testimony, records, and water samples at the festival itself. Coral visits Rosa's grave to rehearse what he'll say. Emotional beat: terror steadied into resolve.

chapters.title: The Centennial Stage
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Mid-ceremony, Coral takes the microphone. He reads Rosa's affidavit aloud as Delia stands beside him and Wes's mother holds up her son's medical file. The crowd's murmur becomes a roar. Emotional beat: the quiet kid, finally loud, voice shaking and unbroken.

chapters.title: Hal Breaks
chapters.summary: Hal's POV (single chapter). Cornered by the evidence and his own conscience, Hal admits the cover-up on stage rather than let his daughter read it in a courtroom later. He resigns on the spot. Emotional beat: villainy revealed as cowardice; the town's idol cracking.

chapters.title: After the Roar
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The vote stalls, the state opens an investigation, and the town turns cold toward Coral — some grateful, some hostile. His locker gets egged; his hand gets shaken twice as often. Emotional beat: the loneliness of truth-telling, softened by the four who stand with him.

chapters.title: Settlement Sunday
chapters.summary: Group POV. Months later: cleanup funded, Rosa's affidavit entered into the record, the school renamed its kitchen garden for her. Delia's tuition debt forgiven publicly. Coral realizes the misfit table has become his family. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined — not money, but courage passed down.

chapters.title: The Last Recipe
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral adds his own card to the box — dated, signed, addressed to whoever comes next — and cooks Rosa's flan for his chosen family in her kitchen. Head up, locker open, voice steady. Emotional beat: full-circle peace; the playlist ends on a song worth singing.
